guide:
How to Use This Planner
• Each module is four instructional weeks. Every module page includes module targets, standards alignment, weekly goals, and Monday-
Friday tasks.
• Weeks 1-3 end with a short weekly quiz. Week 4 ends with a comprehensive module assessment. Use Monday after an assessment for
corrections, reteaching, and reassessment when needed.
• The daily tasks are a teacher-facing roadmap, not a minute-by-minute script. Swap readings, videos, labs, or practice sets while
preserving the stated target and standards.
• Science and social studies tasks emphasize inquiry, source analysis, writing, data interpretation, and projects so that literacy standards
are reinforced across the day.
• Spanish is planned as a novice-level world-language course focused on interpersonal, interpretive, and presentational communication.
Suggested Assessment Weighting
• Daily practice / notebook / participation: 30%
• Weekly quizzes: 25%
• Module comprehensive assessments: 30%
• Projects, presentations, labs, and writing products: 15%
Weekly Quiz Blueprint
• Math: 8-10 items (mostly current-week content + 1-2 spiral-review items).
• ELA: 8-10 items split among grammar/language, spelling/vocabulary, and a short reading/writing item.
• Science/Social Studies: alternate emphasis weekly; 5-8 selected-response/short-response items using diagrams, maps, data, or sources.
• Spanish: 5-10 minute oral/written check (vocabulary, number/date, sentence, or mini-dialogue).
Module Assessment Blueprint
• Math: 20-25 items across the module’s standards; include constructed response.
• ELA: reading passage(s), grammar/language section, spelling/vocabulary, and a short writing task.
• Science: 10-15 items plus one data/model/CER task or practical component.
• Social Studies: 10-15 items plus one map/source/constructed-response task.
